guide

How to open clipboard history on Windows

Press Windows + V to see your clipboard history. If it is your first time, choose Turn on. The history starts collecting new copies after you enable it.

↗guide

How to clear the clipboard on Windows

The current clipboard, Windows + V history and an app’s saved library are different places. Clear the one that contains the information you want to remove.

↗guide

Copy several things. Paste the right one.

You do not need to switch back to the original document for every paste. Collect a few copies, then choose each one from your history.

↗guide

Paste the words. Leave the formatting.

A copied paragraph can bring along a font, background color or link style. Plain-text paste keeps its text while leaving the source styling behind.

↗guide

Back up your clipboard history before you need it.

Use Clipora’s password-encrypted export for a portable backup. Keep the password separately and verify the file before resetting or uninstalling the app.

CLIPORA RESOURCES

Getting started ↗Help & troubleshooting ↗Privacy & data ↗Press kit ↗
  1. Install and open. Get Clipora from Microsoft Store. Local history does not need an app account.
  2. Copy while recording. Start with synthetic text, a link or an image. Recording begins while Clipora runs; it does not import old history from another app.
  3. Choose the destination. Click the input where you want to paste. Press Ctrl+Alt+V, search and click a clip or press Enter.
  4. Pin useful clips. Use the pin button; pinned clips stay at the top. The menu also offers editing, copy, deletion and ordering.
  5. Adjust your workspace. Settings → Appearance controls theme, accent color, density, thumbnails and picker dimensions.
  6. Back up. Backup & restore exports an encrypted library with a password. Keep the password safely; it is not recoverable. Restore merges records and confirmed deletion records may remove matching items.

Keep recording under your control.

Pause before copying sensitive data. Closing the workspace keeps the app in the tray; Quit exits. Enable Start with Windows only if you want recording available at sign-in. Windows can disable startup in its own Settings.

Common limitations

Use manual Ctrl+V when Windows restricts automatic input into an elevated application. File clips store paths, so moving the underlying files can break references. Rapid copies may miss intermediate content. Windows reset/uninstall can remove package data; export a backup first.

Make quick access work your way

Enter pastes the selected clip. Shift+Enter copies it. Alt+Enter pastes plain text; Ctrl+Enter types the selected text. Ctrl+1 through Ctrl+0 selects the first ten results. Escape closes quick access.

Power tools, when you need them

Use offline OCR to extract text from copied images. Reusable snippets can include placeholders. Sequential paste queues support repeated workflows. Trusted C# and VB.NET macros can run full .NET code with your permissions; review code before trusting it. Optional sync starts disabled.

Stay up to date

Open Updates in the workspace, or Settings → General → Updates. Store installations use Microsoft Store updates. Standalone installations link to the Store; transfer your separately stored library using an encrypted backup.
